aoi_name: Liwa (eastern crescent: Wadhil / Mawsil), southern Abu Dhabi

baseline.note: velocities from the Landsat 8/9 OLI network (12 November scenes, 66 pairs); the Landsat 7 scenes (2000-11-27, 2001-11-30) are used only as a long-baseline check

speed_note: speeds are of the 3392 dune windows (480 m) with detected motion (89.7 % of 3782 valid); the other 390 move slower than their detection limit (median 0.97 m/yr) and are not in these statistics. Max detected 5.76 m/yr. uncertainty_myr = median calibrated 1-sigma per component.
wind_agreement_note: mean |heading - RDD| over detected windows, RDD 145.3 deg (MERRA-2 2000-2024). The regime is close to unimodal (RDP/DP 0.594): the field-median heading 165.0 deg is 7.5 deg from the strongest sand-moving mode (toward 157.5 deg) and 19.7 deg from RDD; per-window median difference 19.5 deg. Year-to-year field speeds follow the MERRA-2 drift (r 0.804).

published.reference: Lorenz, Radebaugh, Barnes & Turtle, EGU2016-9369; Lorenz & Radebaugh 2015 (Planetary Dunes Workshop 8003); Pugh, Glennie & Williams 1993 (AAPG abstract)
published.their_value: ~0.1 m/yr for the 50-80 m Liwa megadunes (a field inference from overrun date palms, abstracts only); the smaller northern dunes 'migrate southward more rapidly than the draa' (no number)
published.our_value: megadune and other large-dune bodies: below the detection limit (median limit 0.95 m/yr) for all 37 bodies that could be tracked; small dunes and bedforms: 1.79 m/yr median toward 165 deg (2013-2025)
published.note: Consistent, but not a test of the 0.1 m/yr: that rate is about a tenth of what this method can resolve here, so 'below the detection limit' neither confirms nor contradicts it. What the data do show is the published pattern: motion toward the south-south-east, and small dunes much faster than the megadunes they surround and ride on.

second_dataset.their_value: HLS S30 (Sentinel-2, independent): field median 1.009 m/yr toward 170.3 deg; per-window correlation with Landsat r = 0.424 (E), 0.726 (N); its detection limit 0.792 m/yr, motion detected in 73.0 % of windows. HLS L30 (same Landsat instruments, not independent): 1.155 m/yr toward 163.7 deg, r = 0.444/0.724
second_dataset.our_value: Landsat pan 15 m over the same years: field median 1.656 m/yr toward 162.6 deg (S30 years); 1.741 m/yr toward 165.1 deg (L30 years)
second_dataset.note: HLS S30 (Sentinel-2) agrees on direction (field headings 7.7 deg apart) and partly on the pattern (r 0.424 E, 0.726 N), with lower speeds (1.009 vs 1.656 m/yr). HLS L30 (same Landsat instruments): heading within 1.4 deg, 1.155 vs 1.741 m/yr. Both HLS stacks are registered on the same date-palm farms as Landsat, so they share the possible registration bias described in the limits and do not test it.

data_handling.notes: 4 November candidate scenes rejected in notebook 01 (cloud/shadow/haze/coverage; listed in pipeline/outputs/liwa/scene_rejections.csv); Landsat 7 used only before the 31 May 2003 SLC failure. Clouds/shadows: Landsat QA_PIXEL bits 0-4 (dilated 1 px), HLS Fmask bits 1-3. Of 10403 tracking windows, 3290 lie outside the box and 3307 are mostly non-dune (vegetation, WorldCover, OSM, hand-drawn change areas); of the 3806 dune windows 0.63 % had too few valid pairs. Window-pair observations rejected: 4.15 % (weak match below the false-match threshold, displacement beyond the reliable range, network outliers).

limits: Detected dune windows move a median 1.79 m/yr (10-90 %: 1.22-2.62, max 5.76) toward 165 deg; 10 % of valid dune windows move below the detection limit (median 0.97 m/yr).

These speeds may be overstated by up to ~0.5 m/yr toward the south-south-east. The only stable ground here is date-palm farms, whose apparent drift (toward 335 deg, the anti-sun direction, as growing palm shadows would cause) cannot be checked against unvegetated ground in this box; it is carried in the detection limit, not removed.

Megadune bodies (up to ~110 m of relief) are below the detection limit. The motion in the velocity grid, the dune polygons and the reach years is that of the small dunes and the bedforms riding over the megadunes, not of the megadunes themselves.

Reach years forecast the migration of dune forms (slip-face advance), not wind-blown sand crossing a road, which happens wherever a road borders loose sand, whatever the dunes do (see borders_free_sand in targets.geojson).
At about 1.8 m/yr one 15 m pixel is about 8 years of motion, so reach years for targets near the sand carry an edge uncertainty of +-7.5 m plus the outline uncertainty of the target.
Most targets are not reached by 2050; targets flagged 'sand at edge now' already have migrating sand within that edge uncertainty.
The projection is advection along the measured 2013-2025 motion, assuming those conditions continue; it does not model dune deformation, merging, splitting or growth.
Vegetation, windbreaks, sand fences, levelling, construction and climate change alter the outcome; many farm edges here are walled.
Motion is measured in 480 m windows: it is the motion of the small dunes (spacing ~85-115 m) and sand sheets inside, not of a single dune body.
Only 17 dunes (13-31 m high) are outlined from NASADEM (February 2000) at bedform scale; they are medium dunes, mostly in the northern field, not megadunes.
The Sentinel-2 (HLS S30) check agrees on direction with lower speeds, but shares the farm-based registration and so cannot test the registration caveat.
The published ~0.1 m/yr for the megadunes is a field inference far below this method's detection limit here: no numeric comparison is possible.
MERRA-2 wind is a ~0.5 x 0.625 deg reanalysis of hourly means; absolute drift potential is approximate.
Farm targets are vegetated plots (HLS NDVI, last year) plus OSM farmland; built-up targets are OSM buildings and residential areas; unmapped or abandoned plots are not targets.
Results are valid for this box (the eastern Liwa crescent, not Liwa town) and 2013-2025 only; nothing outside the box is assessed.

threat.reach_definition: Migrating dune sand (free sand inside a window whose dune-form migration is detected), carried along its measured heading at its measured speed, arrives at the edge of the target footprint (road: OSM centre line +- class half width incl. shoulders; farm: HLS vegetated outline; built-up: OSM outline).
excludes: wind-blown sand crossing or settling on a target
motion below the detection limit (no direction: never a hit)
dune deformation, merging, growth, levelling or stabilisation
threat.speeds: median = measured window speed v; fast = v + sigma; slow = v - sigma (sigma = calibrated per-component 1-sigma; 84th/16th percentiles of the speed)
threat.years: hit_year_min = floor(t0 + gap_lo / fast); hit_year_max = ceil(t0 + gap_hi / slow); gap = distance from the source pixel centre to the footprint along the heading minus 7.5 m, +-(7.5 m + outline uncertainty: roads/buildings 5 m, farms 15 m); t0 = 2025-11-08; earliest over all sand reaching the target; null if the fast case does not arrive by 2100
